observations: Two bacterial cells with no drawn nucleus; both contain the same circular plasmid symbol.
Green promoter arrow precedes a blue DNA segment; mRNA passes between the two purple ribosomal subunits on the left.
Solid black left-to-right process arrows separate plasmid, transcript/ribosome, and orange folded target protein.
Right-hand dashed process arrow ends in a red X and the bounded label Kein Zielprotein.
Promotor, Plasmid, mRNA, Ribosom and Zielprotein labels are attached to the correct visible objects.
At the actual supplied 360-pixel raster size I can read DNA allein genügt nicht, Signal erkannt, Signal nicht erkannt and Kein Zielprotein without enlarging it.
Promotor, Plasmid, mRNA, Ribosom and Zielprotein are smaller but individually decipherable; the colored objects and short directional arrows remain distinct.
Neither panel is clipped; the process and the failure contrast do not require reading a dense paragraph.
All labels and arrowheads are readable at the actual supplied 680-pixel raster size.
The mRNA remains visibly threaded through the ribosome, and the target protein is distinct from the transcript.
Panel framing, circular plasmids and bounded right-hand failure remain visible without cropping.
